notes: Object insert. 'Gothic attests farjoskip' makes it a Gothic word through the catalogue: attested_in is the inverse of attests_word and a subproperty of word_of_language (RELATIONS.md, 2026-10-30), so the local rule attests_word -> word_of_language is gone. q1's prompt states that the word is attested in one language only (given, since 2026-10-31; before, the file put this presupposition of a definite description in given without the prompt saying it). The Codex Argenteus is a translation; its language is written_in_language, which covers a manuscript's or translation's language since 2026-10-30.

queries.not_checked: fol: compares two words' language branches

fol.notes: As grammar-insert-0002. The 'no' needs each word to have one language (Gothic for 'farjoskip', English for 'ferry'); the chain takes this for granted, so both are presuppositions.

local.branch_of: the branch of a language family a language belongs to (one branch per language)

words.says: The two words are spelled 'farjoskip' and 'ferry'.

attests_def.says: A word a language attests is a word of that language.
attests_def.z3: ForAll([l, w], Implies(attests_word(l, w), word_of_language(w, l)))

gothic_eg.says: Gothic is an East Germanic language.

english_wg.says: English is a West Germanic language.

ferry_english.says: The English word 'ferry' is a word of English.

farjoskip_one_language.says: 'Farjoskip' is a word of one language only. (closed world)

ferry_one_language.says: 'Ferry' is a word of English only. (closed world)

queries.ask: Exists([l, l2], And(word_of_language(farjoskip, l), word_of_language(ferry, l2), branch_of(l) == branch_of(l2)))

label_corrections.why: 'Same branch' is a join through a functional branch relation (ALCOI with nominals); the 'no' needs the two one-language presuppositions as 'only' restrictions.
